text.p: Italian bonds and futures ended lower, wiping out earlier gains which took the Btp Liffe March contract up to a new record high of 131.27, on a general wave of profit-taking, which also affected Milan stocks, and in line with easier U.S. Treasuries.

Traders said the market was cautiously watching developments on U.S. debt markets and was less concerned with domestic events, although Btps began slipping after today's mid-month auction of 2.0 trillion lire worth of 7.75 percent 10-year Btps where the gross yield fell to 7.17 percent from a previous 7.47.
Spread over 10-year bunds widened to 159 bps from early 153.
"There were a few peaks and troughs today but the auction did have an effect," one London futures trader said.

"The wave of profit-taking has affected all the markets, dollar, T-bond and other European exchanges, but it is hard to pinpoint the epicentre of the quake," another dealer said. "And really a March Btp fall after recent highs is normal," he added.

One trader said the correction phase started in the afternoon from 131.27 peaks had set first major support at 130.40. "But this could be just a limited correction after the major rally over the last couple of sessions," he said.
"Alarm bells won't start ringing until we see a fall below 130.00," another said.
This trader said selling on the cash bond market had not been massive. "This morning people were selling paper to buy futures but volumes have been less than in past sessions," he added.
The July 2006 Btp ended 12 bps down at 110.32 after a high at 110.95. The 10-year yield was 7.35 percent after a session minimum below 7.30 percent.
